predecessors.name: Duchy of Croatia
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Croatia of Tomislav's Croats of Dalmatia and Pannonia, raised to a kingdom c.

successors.name: Croatia in union with Hungary
successors.text: the Kingdom of Croatia in union with Hungary after Coloman's coronation at Biograd in 1102: the kingdom's last Cliopatria shape, 1094-1098

ledger.x: 925: Tomislav is crowned King of the Croats and unites Pannonia and Dalmatia.

c. 925: Croatia keeps its northern borders against the Magyars and gains part of the former Pannonian duchy. 'Croatia kept its northern borders and gained part of the former Pannonian duchy, including Sisak'; the Hungarian conflict is 'not precisely dated'.
926: Tomislav destroys Simeon's army under Alogobotur.
927: Simeon dies and peace is restored.
980: page silent.
1000: Venice's Orseolo takes the Adriatic.
1018: Venice defeats Kresimir III; the kingdom becomes a Byzantine vassal until 1025.
1018: the Dalmatian cities pass out of Croatian hands.
1050: the Narentine duke becomes a vassal of Stjepan I.
1060: Petar Kresimir IV takes the Dalmatian city-states.
1067: Ulric I of Carniola occupies the Kvarner coast and eastern Istria.
1069: Byzantium recognises Petar Kresimir IV in Dalmatia.
1074: Zvonimir, then ban, has liberated the Kvarner coast and Istria by the end of Kresimir's reign.
1074: the Normans seize Kresimir and the cities.
ledger.cp: Normans of Apulia (Count Amico of Giovinazzo)

ledger.x: 1075: Venice expels the Normans and holds the cities.
1085: Byzantium hands its rights in Dalmatia to Venice.
1085: Venice holds the Dalmatian cities.
1091: Ladislaus of Hungary conquers Slavonia.
1091: the war for the rest of Croatia begins.
1097: Coloman defeats the last native king at Gvozd.
1102: Coloman is crowned king of Croatia at Biograd and Croatia enters union with Hungary.
1102: the Narentine vassalage lapses with the kingdom.

wars.name: Croatian-Bulgarian war of 926
wars.outcome: Croatian victory over Alogobotur's army in 926; peace restored in 927 after Simeon's death through papal legates; no change of border.

wars.name: Croatian-Hungarian conflict under Tomislav
wars.outcome: Undated Hungarian war; Croatia kept its northern borders and gained part of the former Pannonian duchy including Sisak.

wars.name: Venetian expedition and the Dalmatian cities
wars.outcome: Orseolo's fleet takes the eastern Adriatic after 1000; Kresimir III wins back some cities until Venice defeats him in 1018 and Croatia becomes a Byzantine vassal until 1025.

wars.name: Norman invasion of Dalmatia (Amico of Giovinazzo)
wars.outcome: Kresimir IV captured and ransomed with Zadar, Split, Trogir, Biograd and Nin; Venice expels the Normans in February 1075 and keeps the cities.

wars.name: Norman invasion of the Byzantine Empire (Guiscard), Croatian naval aid
wars.outcome: Zvonimir, bound by his pledge to the Holy See, sent naval troops to the Normans; in 1085 Byzantium transferred its Dalmatian rights to Venice.

wars.name: Hungarian conquest of Croatia
wars.outcome: Ladislaus takes Slavonia in 1091; Almos governs the occupied part until 1095; Petar Snacic is elected king in 1093 and killed at Gvozd in 1097; Coloman is crowned at Biograd in 1102.

certainty.note: Medieval Croatia's frontiers in Bosnia, Slavonia and the Dalmatian hinterland are approximate (historians disagree, per the Tomislav page); no treaty line exists.
